extracted.intended_audience: general readers / SNL and pop-culture fans
extracted.subtask_description: Identify the factors that determine whether a performer succeeds or is fired on Saturday Night Live (fit for sketch-comedy television), based on actors' retrospective accounts. Focuses on performer skills, show dynamics, and managerial practices that influence retention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suitability for rapid‑fire sketch comedy
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether a performer is 'suited' to the fast-paced, improv-heavy demands of SNL—e.g., ability to do impressions, create catchphrases, and work in rapid sketch environments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Robert Downey Jr. described himself as 'ill‑suited' and 'not somebody who was going to come up with a catchphrase...do impressions...not of that ilk of The Groundlings.' The page implies that improv/training with groups like The Groundlings and comfort with rapid turnaround are important predictors of success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to create breakout characters or catchphrases
rubrics_metrics.description: Having recognizable recurring characters or catchphrases that connect with audiences and give a performer a distinct SNL identity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anthony Michael Hall said he 'didn't even have any breakout characters or anything like that.' The lack of breakout material is presented as a reason a performer might not 'have a breakout season' and thus be let go.

rubrics_metrics.name: Being used by the show / writers (fit with assigned material)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the show's writers and producers write material that utilizes a performer’s strengths rather than pigeonholing them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Jay Pharoah said 'SNL puts people into boxes' and that performers may feel 'they don't use you.' Poor utilization (writers not writing for a performer's talents) can contribute to dissatisfaction and termination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transferability of other acting fame/skills to sketch comedy
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether prior success in film or dramatic acting translates into sketch‑comedy ability; star power alone does not guarantee fit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Several examples (Robert Downey Jr., Joan Cusack, Anthony Michael Hall) show established movie actors who were 'ill‑suited' or 'miserable' on SNL, indicating that different skill sets are required for sketch work versus film acting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relationship with writers and workplace dynamics
rubrics_metrics.description: Interactions and relationships with writers and cast influence a performer's experience and job security (e.g., being disliked by writers can harm standing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gilbert Gottfried said 'the writers hated me' and recounted negative experiences; strained relationships with writers (or being the target of poor sketches) are presented as contributing factors to being fired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show performance / ratings context
rubrics_metrics.description: The overall popularity and ratings of the show or a particular season can lead to cast changes; performers may be dismissed following 'ratings‑challenged' seasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adam Sandler and Chris Farley were dismissed 'after five ratings‑challenged seasons,' suggesting managerial decisions about cast turnover are influenced by the show's performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal fit and well‑being in the SNL environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether a performer personally adapts to the SNL workload and culture (miserable/illness from the experience can indicate poor fit).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Joan Cusack said 'It wasn't working... I was miserable. I think I wound up in the hospital, actually,' implying that personal hardship or inability to cope with the environment is a factor in short tenures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Managerial norms for firing and notification
rubrics_metrics.description: How firings are communicated and handled by leadership—Lorne Michaels is known for avoiding direct bad‑news conversations; some performers learn of their firing indirectly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article notes 'Lorne Michaels does not like to give bad news' and recounts Gilbert Gottfried learning he was fired from a fan letter; also that 'not-ready-for-primetime players do not know when they’ve been fired.' This procedural norm affects performers' experience but is distinct from performance criteria.
